question: None shared. P-85 builds binary classifiers for MCI vs NC (also MCI vs SCD and SCD vs NC) from task-state prefrontal fNIRS connectivity plus cognitive-scale scores and completion times, in a Zhejiang/Shanghai sample. P-86 builds one 3-class AD / MCI / normal-aging classifier on T1 structural MRI (NACC 88%, ADNI 8%, Hanyang 4%) and reports one-vs-rest AUCs. The contrast differs (MCI vs NC against MCI vs the rest of an AD/MCI/normal sample), and the channels differ (fNIRS + questionnaire against MRI), with no shared channel.
metric: Mismatch: binary ROC-AUC / accuracy (P-85) against one-vs-rest AUC and per-class metrics inside a 3-class task (P-86). The record's 88% and 87% carry no metric type and match no printed figure for the designs it names.

figures.P-85: MCI vs NC: best accuracy 0.920; best AUC 0.970 (95% CI 0.946-0.993), 5-fold CV on 48 NC + 90 MCI retained for analysis.
figures.P-86: MCI one-vs-rest AUC in the 3-class task: combined CNN-GAT 0.719 +- 0.015 (fold SD; 72.3% in the Results text), CNN 0.696, GAT 0.639; stratified 5-fold CV on 1,900 scans.

matched_figure_check: Not applicable: neither paper reports the other's contrast or channel. P-85 has no MRI and no 3-class result; P-86 has no binary MCI-vs-NC result and no fNIRS.
performance_validity: P-85's best MCI-vs-NC figure (AUC 0.970, 95% CI 0.946-0.993) meets the Section 3.5 exclusion: internal 5-fold CV on 138 participants with no external cohort. P-86 (MCI AUC 0.719) does not.
reason: The two papers do not share a clinical question or a channel. P-85 separates MCI from controls with fNIRS and cognitive scales; P-86 scores MCI against the rest of a 3-class AD/MCI/normal sample from structural MRI. P-85's best figure also meets the performance-validity exclusion. The recorded disagreement (attention fusion at 88% vs concatenation + SVM at 87% on the same ADNI cohort) misreads both papers. P-85 has no attention model and is not ADNI; P-86 has no SVM and is mostly NACC. The record itself calls the one-point gap noise.

quotes.quote: Accuracies of 92.0 % for MCI vs. NC, 80.0 % for MCI vs. SCD, and 76.1 % for SCD vs. NC were achieved, and the highest AUC values were 97.0 % (95 % CI: 94.6 %-99.3 %) for MCI vs. NC
Consequently, 203 participants, including 48 NC volunteers (NC group), 65 SCD individuals (SCD group), and 90 MCI individuals (MCI group) were finally included for the FC analysis.
Herein, a combined CNN–GAT framework was constructed for the classification of AD, MCI and normal aging.
the AUC increased to 86.5 % for AD and 72.3 % for MCI
